newsitem.title: DENMARK: DANISH BONDS SET TO HOLD LEVELS IN QUIET MARKET.
newsitem.headline: DANISH BONDS SET TO HOLD LEVELS IN QUIET MARKET.

text.p: Danish bond prices were slightly lower in early trading on Thursday with dealers expecting levels to hold in a quiet summer market.
"It looks like prices will stick around current levels all day. The German market seems to have stabilised," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.12 point from Wednesday's close at 112.57, yielding 6.08 percent at 0750 GMT. The seven percent 2007 bond, due to take over as benchmark on September 1, slipped 0.11 point to 195.44, with yield at 6.27 percent.
The 2007's 10 year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 58 bps overnight.
The Danish crown traded at 3.8090, slightly down from Wednesday's 3.8085 close. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652
